root_idea.summary: The root centers on gathering into a body and the support or aid that such a body provides.
root_idea.development: This orientation extends from assembled supporters to an army or host, and in Classical Arabic to a military district from which forces were gathered. The related senses جَنَدٌ, “a town,” and الْجَنَدُ, “rough stony ground,” are separately reported, with their connection to the root principle treated as uncertain.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The sole Quran-attested form group is presented under the normalized singular collective citation form جُنْدٌ.

senses.definition: A gathered host or force: an army, military body, or body of troops.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quran uses the collective singular جُنْد and its plural جُنُود for human armies and for hosts or forces associated with God or other beings, including unseen forces. The form may therefore denote a military army or a broader marshalled host.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To collect or assemble armies, military forces, or troops.
To take or prepare an army or military force for oneself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form V verb; the force is acquired or made ready for the subject’s use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A single trooper, soldier, or auxiliary.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun-of-unity use, distinguished from the collective sense “army” or “military force.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: A kind or species of creatures or created things considered as a distinct body.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used for a kind regarded separately from other kinds; the usage can be extended figuratively to creatures that serve a purpose as auxiliaries.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A city together with its territory, especially a military district or province of Syria.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Syrian administrative usage includes the traditionally enumerated military districts, whose forces were collected there; the plural is أَجْنَادٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Pertaining to a Syrian جُنْد, or military district.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Adjectival nisbah formation referring specifically to the Syrian district sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A collected or organized army or military force.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional collocation emphasizing that the force has been gathered together.
A separately reported vocalized lexical item; its relation to the gathering-and-support sense is not established here.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rough, hard ground containing white stones.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical source allows that this may belong to the same semantic family, but also proposes derivation by substitution from جَلَدٌ; the etymological relationship is therefore uncertain.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Form II collection or assembly of armies.
Form V taking or preparing an army for oneself.
Collective army or force and noun-of-unity soldier or auxiliary uses.
Kind or species of created things regarded as a separate body.
Adjectival sense relating to a Syrian جُنْد.
Conventional expression for a collected army or military force.

cautions: The Quranic entry treats جُنْدٌ and its plural جُنُودٌ primarily as collective hosts or forces; the individual soldier sense is separately attested in broader Classical Arabic evidence.
The reported connection of جَنَدٌ or الْجَنَدُ with the root’s gathering-and-support principle is uncertain in the lexical evidence.
